edits.text: - Does translating the two sides separately still add up to the whole sentence? This cohesion check is worst when the cut splits a contiguous multi-character unit (a tight verb–object sequence, a '…的…' modifier, a foreign-script or Romanized name, or a numeral+measure group) or when the following material contains scope-bearing modifiers whose attachment will change meaning; it is milder when the following phrase is an independent adjunct or optional elaboration that can be translated apart, and milder still when the marker falls immediately after such a unit so the unit remains intact.
edits._was: - Does translating the two sides separately still add up to the whole sentence? This cohesion check is worst when the following material contains scope-bearing modifiers whose attachment will change meaning (long 的-modifiers, coverb scope, or complements that resolve prior references); it is mild when the following phrase is an independent adjunct or optional elaboration that can be translated apart and joined without loss.

edits.text: When one candidate splits a tight multi-character unit (verb–object, a '…的…' modifier, foreign name, or numeral+measure) and another candidate immediately follows that unit, prefer the latter marker that keeps the unit intact.
edits._was: - When one marker lies inside a named multiword unit (foreign sequence or numeral+measure) and another marker immediately follows that unit, prefer the latter marker that keeps the unit intact.

edits.text: - Does the marker fall immediately before the main lexical verb or an essential clausal complement when the preceding segment contains no predicate? This is most severe when the pre-cut stretch is a nominal or modifier-only fragment (no verb, auxiliary, copula, aspect marker, or other predicate) so that the fragment is unanchored, contradictory, or uninterpretable without the continuation; it is mild when the pre-cut stretch already contains a clear predicate (auxiliary, copula, aspect particle, or main verb) or when the following material is an optional adjunct, parenthetical, or clarifying elaboration that does not complete the clause.
edits._was: - Does the following material complete or leave unresolved a predicate or an argument required to understand the clause so far? This is severe if an essential object, complement, or aspect/voice marker appears only after the cut (so the pre-cut fragment lacks the predicate or patient), and milder if only optional temporal or manner adjuncts follow.
